notes:
Summary: Cerise is an enterprise retail personalization provider exploring Redwood Dedicated for latency-critical reranking + real-time personalization. They have a strict need for fixed throughput guarantees and clear burst policies to protect UX during seasonal spikes.

Recent activity:
- 2026-02-12 kickoff (ff_2026-02-12_cerise_intro): intro AE/SE/CTO, high-level requirements captured.
- 2026-02-26 perf kickoff (ff_2026-02-26_perf_kickoff): agreed on POC scenarios (rerank pipeline, personalization microservice, embeddings index refresh).
- 2026-03-01 security touchpoint (ff_2026-03-01_security_review): SSO/KMS/audit logging questions logged. SEC ticket opened (SEC-1198).
- 2026-03-02 follow-up: sent draft SOW and pricing option matrix (gmail thread:1792a1ef_cerise_pricing).

Workload & performance requirements (explicit asks):
- Primary workload: reranking (batch of top-N candidates) + real-time personalization chat snippets. Typical request token size: 30-80 tokens.
- Peak QPS target: 1,000 requests/sec for reranking flow (avg 45 tokens/request) -> target ~45k tokens/sec sustained at peak retail hours.
- Minimum guaranteed throughput: Cerise asks for a commercial guarantee of 40k tokens/sec dedicated baseline (min tokens/sec).
- Concurrency cap: want hard cap at 400 concurrent inference streams for chat endpoints; reranking can be horizontally queued.
- Burst policy: need 2.5x burst capacity for up to 10 minutes (for flash sales), with automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants after burst budget is exhausted.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 120ms for chat (short-turn responses), p95 <= 250ms for reranking; p99 targets are softer but should be <500ms for both.
- Availability SLO: 99.9% monthly for dedicated pool.

Model & runtime preferences:
- Preference for open Llama-family quantized variants (to match on-prem licensing) and ability to fall back to smaller low-latency variants when under contention.
- Expectation: each A100-like GPU (8x reserved initially) should deliver ~4k-6k tokens/sec for their tuned Llama-variant under our batching profile; they request Redwood to map tokens/sec -> number of reserved GPUs in SOW with margin.
- KV cache warmup: want guidance on pre-warm strategies and priming to avoid cold-start penalties during burst windows.

Operational requirements & security:
- VPC peering + private control plane required; EU data residency for EU customer subset (must provide region pinning).
- Audit logs retained 12 months, KMS integration mandatory, SSO/SAML with SCIM provisioning.
- Compliance pack review next week (drive doc link provided).

Commercial / SLA negotiation points:
- Cerise wants a contractual minimum tokens/sec with credits for missed tokens/sec on a monthly basis (formula requested).
- They prefer deterministic concurrency caps rather than best-effort; require explicit behavior when cap is reached (queue vs reject vs degrade).
- Burst billing model: prefer prepaid burst credits included in committed ARR rather than pay-as-you-go to avoid CFO pushback during seasonal spikes.
- Discount tiers tied to committed GPU count and length of term (12/24/36 months).

Open questions / blockers:
- Legal wants explicit example calculation for "missed tokens/sec" SLA credit.
- CFO wants side-by-side for Dedicated vs Dedicated+Private (cost + ops delta).
- Security needs final network diagram and assurance on on-prem variant (if chosen) for air-gapped storefronts.

Customer quotes / call snippets:
- CTO: "If we cannot guarantee rerank latency at peak we lose conversions; throughput guarantees are table stakes."
- Head of Infra: "We will only sign if there's a clear burst model that doesn't break the billing runbook."

Next steps (short):
- SE to run 48-hour synthetic throughput verification with Redwood-provided perf harness (Marco Liu to schedule; window target 2026-03-18 to 2026-03-19).
- AE to circulate SOW with GPU->tokens/sec table and SLA sample language (Nina to send v2 by 2026-03-12).
- Legal/Sales ops sync to draft SLA credit formula and finalize procurement checklist (expected by 2026-03-25).

POC success criteria (customer defined):
- Sustained 40k tokens/sec for 4 hours with p95 latencies within targets.
- Seamless 2.5x burst ability for at least one 10-minute window during test.
- VPC peering validated and audit logs visible in customer console.

Notes on uniqueness: Cerise emphasizes deterministic concurrency behavior and prepaid burst credits. They are more conservative on p95 latency and want explicit GPU->throughput mapping in contract (uncommon ask).
